title: Sun star
summary: Turn the sun into a sharp star burst.

media.alt: Low sun forming a star of rays over a rocky shore

steps: Find an edge to hide the sun behind: a tree, building, rock or the horizon.
Move until the edge covers about **half** the sun.
Shift a few centimetres back and forth until the star looks strongest.
Underexpose a little to keep the sky colour. Bracket if unsure.

after.text: Don't look at the sun through an optical viewfinder. Use the screen.

steps: **Shooting 2 › Expo.comp./AEB:** start at **−1** to keep the sky's colour. AEB (bracketing) is on the same screen.
Hide about half the sun behind an edge and move a few centimetres until the star is strongest.
Turn on **Playback 5 › Highlight alert** and check what blinks after each shot.
Keep it brief: the manual warns that pointing the camera at the sun can damage the sensor. Cap the lens between shots.
canon-r10.note: The R10's viewfinder is electronic, so it's safe for your eye, but the sensor still takes the heat.
